messages:
pranav: Heads-up — Obsidian (dedicated) is seeing a ~15% p95 tail latency regression since the kernel-selector change last night. Profiling shows more KV cache misses and smaller formed batches. @amanda can you triage?

amanda: on it. do we have the profile + a sample request trace?

pranav: attaching short snippet (from perf agent):
```
kernel_selector: v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0
median_batch_size: 6 -> 4
p95_latency_ms: 92 -> 108
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.07 -> 0.18
cpu_util_gpu_util: 42% / 78% -> 33% / 80%
```

julia: looks like the new kernel path favors smaller micro-batches (kernel fusion tradeoff). that + KV thrash explains lower batching efficiency. any change in request size distribution for Obsidian?

ken: Obsidian traffic is steady; median request tokens ~340, but they had a few long-shot evals (2k tokens) earlier today which probably pushed KV eviction.

amanda: propose short-term: raise the token_budget_target for Obsidian slice and enforce a queue cap to avoid underfilled GPU slices. suggested quick patch:
```json
{
  "customer": "obsidian",
  "slice_policy": {
    "token_budget_target": 12000,
    "max_queue_depth": 32,
    "min_batch_fill_ms": 12,
    "kv_prefetch": "aggressive"
  }
}
```

li: quick note — raising token_budget_target will increase per-slice latency SLO risk for small requests unless we also bump min_batch_fill_ms. maybe set min_batch_fill_ms to 8-15ms depending on latency SLO.

amanda: good call. Obsidian agreed to a softer p95 target (they prefer throughput/cost). propose min_batch_fill_ms = 14ms and max_queue_depth 48.

pranav: can we run a canary? patch runtime routing to only apply to obsidian-dedicated pool for next 2h. capture kernel selection metrics + per-slice batch sizes.

ken: I'll spin canary: `./deploy-canary --pool obsidian-dedicated --config obsidian-slotting-v1`

sre-bot: deploy started by ken at 2045679120. Canary will run on 2 nodes (gpus: A100x2) with sampling 10%. Logs forwarded to #eng-runtime-perf.

julia: one more thing — we should adjust kernel-selector heuristics: add a delta floor for kernel that underfills batches less than 4 tokens. that prevents switching to fused kernels when it hurts batching. i'll open a tiny PR.

amanda: plan summary: 1) canary config (token_budget_target=12000, min_batch_fill_ms=14, max_queue_depth=48, kv_prefetch=aggressive) 2) runtime kernel-selector tweak PR from julia 3) monitor p50/p95, kv_miss_rate, median_batch_size for 3h 4) rollback if p95 > baseline + 10%

pranav: perfect. set the canary window to 3h and mark for postmortem if no improvement. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ken: canary up at 2045679155. linking perf dash: https://perf.redwoodinfra/internal/dash?run=2045679155

amanda: logging results into ticket INF-4892, will paste final numbers there.

sre-bot: canary finished at 2045679320. summary: median_batch_size -> 5 (from 4), p95_latency down 9%, kv_cache_miss_rate down to 0.09. Full metrics in ticket INF-4892.

pranav: great — roll to obsidian pool with the new config and keep kernel-selector change gated until we validate across multiple customers.

amanda: deploying to obsidian pool now, ETA 15m.

ken: deployed. monitoring looks stable so far.
